entries.appliesTo: utilization review organizations and health carriers (prior authorization and claim review)

dutySources.human-review: § 514F.8A(2)(a) — 'The decision to deny or downgrade the request is made by either of the following: (1) A qualified reviewer, if the health care provider requesting prior authorization is a physician. (2) A clinical peer, if the health care provider requesting prior authorization is not a physician.'

exposure.enforcer: commissioner-of-insurance (remedies routed through Iowa Code chapters 505 and 507B)

sources.aiSoleBasis: § 514F.8(2A) — 'a utilization review organization shall not use an artificial intelligence-based algorithm or system as the sole basis for the utilization review organization’s decision to deny, delay, or downgrade the prior authorization request'
sources.decisionsCovered: § 514F.8(2A) — 'for a prior authorization request for a health care service based on medical necessity'
sources.humanReview: § 514F.8A(2)(a) — 'The decision to deny or downgrade the request is made by either of the following: (1) A qualified reviewer, if the health care provider requesting prior authorization is a physician.'
sources.enforcer: § 514F.8E — 'The remedy for noncompliance with section 514F.8, 514F.8A, 514F.8B, 514F.8C, or 514F.8D shall be those remedies authorized by chapters 505 and 507B pursuant to the procedures set forth in sections 507B.6, 507B.7, and 507B.8.'

flags: Omnibus health bill; AI provision is narrow: only § 514F.8(2A) addresses AI ('may use an artificial intelligence-based algorithm or system to provide an initial review of a request for prior authorization' but not as sole basis for deny/delay/downgrade of a medical-necessity request). All other provisions are non-AI insurance/health regulation.

humanReview enum is lossy: human decision-makers are required both for the final denial/downgrade determination (§ 514F.8A(2)(a)) and on appeal by a different qualified reviewer or clinical peer (§ 514F.8A(4)(a)-(b) — 'A qualified reviewer or clinical peer involved in the initial denial or downgrade determination … shall not conduct the appeal'); coded as required-final per closest-single-enum rule.

appealDays not coded: the 30-calendar-day appeal window in § 514F.8C(2)(c) ('may appeal the adverse determination no later than thirty calendar days') applies to claim-payment audit determinations, not AI/prior-authorization decisions; the prior-authorization appeal in § 514F.8A(4) states no filing deadline.

Additional exposure not capturable in params: § 514F.8E — 'the commissioner of insurance may also suspend a utilization review organization’s authority to conduct utilization review' upon a pattern or practice of noncompliance; § 514F.8C(2)(e) — audit violations require the claim to be 'approved … and promptly paid, including interest at the rate of ten percent per annum'.

Non-coded divisions fitting no family: Division I § 514F.8D health-carrier standards of conduct (no referral penalties, no interference in staffing, negotiation opportunity); Division II § 514F.8B and Division III §§ 249A.5/249A.6/514I.13 prior-authorization exemptions (cancer screenings, emergency conditions) and mandatory electronic prior-auth submission — Division III binds the department of health and human services and Medicaid/Hawki managed care organizations; Division IV certificate-of-need amendments (Iowa Code ch. 135) contain no AI provisions.

Peer-review duties in § 514F.8A (denial statement signed by reviewer, written attestation of reviewer credentials, appeals-process explanation, 7-business-day peer consultation on request) fit no listed duty key beyond human-review; noted here rather than improvised.
Applicability: § 514F.8A(5) — 'This section applies to requests for prior authorization made on or after January 1, 2027.'
